utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, good afternoon to you. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. When we go through the preliminaries, if you could kindly find out how long Mr. Meek has been cross-examining the witness. Yes, usual advisory to the accused. Any problems with interpretation, please draw our attention straight away. I see that there's no major change -- there are no major changes. The Prosecution is in full house. Any preliminaries? None. Only thing is, Mr. McCloskey, in relation to the issues following the separation of Tolimir and Trbic, there was one objection raised by the Defence that hasn't been addressed as yet. Strictly speaking, you had until today to do that. Maybe -- I think in order to save time I will get the -- one of my staff to -- to contact you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One of our staff will contact you during the first break, okay. And if there is a need for a short extension, small extension, we'll probably grant it. So any preliminaries? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We hope not to have any problem with our next witness, but we've -- there may be a problem. I hate to offer problems that don't yet exist. The witness wants to testify publicly and we noticed that he had protective measures last time, so the appeals court is, we think, about ready to sign off on that but we didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know, I'm fully aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was about to raise the matter yesterday, but I stopped short of that in anticipation of this morning, I would come and find the decision on my -- which hasn't been the case. But it's anticipated any moment, but should it not arrive by the time the witness is to start his evidence, then I think there is another way out, there's another way we can handle it. So we'll wait, I think, because I'm confident we'll have the Appeals Chamber's decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And given the estimates of the next -- well, both the witnesses, the Defence and myself have spoken, it would be best for everyone if we just planned Mr. Ruez to be next week, though of course you make that decision. I mentioned that yesterday and we weren't sure exactly if you had made a decision on that or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. You mentioned it yesterday and we decided independently irrespective of that. We just decided yesterday not to lose the three-quarters of an hour that we had available. So we'll decide the rest during the first break and we will let you know. Any further matters? None. Usher, if you could kindly usher in the witness, please. Right, Mr. Meek, you still have the floor. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Oric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek is going to continue with his cross- examination, and then he will be followed by other Defence counsel for other accused. Mr. Meek, he is all yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Oric, how are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I'm fine. Thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: A couple of questions, sir. Yesterday at page 27 of the transcript, line 14 -- 13 and 14 when you were speaking about being in the -- arriving -- or being at the gymnasium at the school, you testified that you were talking to your cousin and that you heard somebody say: There's Mladic. Do you recall that testimony, Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: To clarify you stated: "I lifted my head and we saw him in the corridor at the entrance to the sports hall." My question, Mr. Oric, is: Did you actually see him with your own eyes or were you told that he was standing at the entrance to the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now -- and you've already testified as to your military duties throughout your lifetime, and I know we're familiar with that. I want to ask a few questions about Ramir Becirovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Becirovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Becirovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, you know who I'm speaking of; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Who was, to your knowledge, his commander?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And it's my understanding then that he was the supreme commander in Srebrenica at the time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Now yesterday you testified at page 44 between line 4 and 5 when you were speaking about your escape, you mentioned a gentleman by the name of Hurem Suljic. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did Hurem go with you all the way to the free zone?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And had you known him prior to that date?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And how many days, approximately, did it take you and Hurem to arrive at the free zone?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the seventh day, we arrived to the free territory from the point of the place of the execution, together on the eleventh day, as of the day Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Oric, if Hurem Suljic is related to Osman Suljic from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you know or have you ever heard of Osman Suljic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of him, but I never met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And could you tell the Chamber what position he held in 1995 in Srebrenica or Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you know that he was the president of the Srebrenica Executive Council in 1995, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Oric, and I know that you've given many statements to different agencies and different investigators over these last 11 years. I want to know whether you recall giving one -- an interview, excuse me, on or about the 11th day of October, 1998, in your own home?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. But you recall giving an interview where Mr. McCloskey, the Prosecutor over here sitting in the middle, an investigator by the name of Jan Kruszewski, and you had an interpreter named Kanita Halilovic and they came to your home at approximately 3.00 in the afternoon? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, I'm looking at a report, but you've never seen it so I'm not going to show it to you, that's been drafted by the investigator John or Jan Kruszewski. And during that interview, Mr. Oric -- the ERN number on that is 00676049 for the Trial Chamber. Thank you. Do you recall discussing that day with Mr. McCloskey, with Jan Kruszewski, the investigator, that you woke up at the railroad tracks behind you, about 20 metres from you was an embankment of the railroad, that you told them that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I stood up the railway tracks were behind me. I can remember that. The tracks were behind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you also --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The embankment and the railway tracks were behind my back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you recall telling them on that day that that the distance from the school to the site and the meadow where the killings took place was five to six minutes?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have said it, but that was an estimate. I didn't have a watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you also recall telling them that you had been told about the location of the execution site only after you reached the free territory and not before?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I arrived to the free territory, I described it and then they told me it was near Gornji Grbavica. I didn't know the exact name of the village and then it was established, the execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And who is "they" that told you it was near Gornji Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the command, in Sapna, on the free territory. When I was giving my statement, this is when they told me that this was on that particular site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And, Mr. Oric, can you tell me approximately when they told you the location of this execution site. Was it the first day of your arrival? The second day? The first week, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the next day when I recovered. It was then that I gave my statement, and then they told me that according to the map this could be the location. They concluded this from my description of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, in your nine days or so with Hurem Suljic, did you discuss your family and those sort of things while you were travelling to the free zone? And if so, sir, did he ever mention to you that he was related to Osman Suljic in any fashion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why don't you skip this and go to the next question. I think he's answered it already, that he was not aware of that, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So then I understand, Mr. Oric, that approximately 10 to 11 days after the killings took place, the command in the free zone informed you of the location of the site where it occurred. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I gave the statement in the free territory, when I explained, they said that it could be near Gornji Grbavica. I didn't know the terrain, but I described where I went and they said that this location could be near Gornji Grbavica, near a hamlet. They mentioned the name. I am not familiar with this terrain, but they were because the refugees came from these -- from this area, from Krizevici and other villages in the area. So they said the -- they gave an estimate of the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Oric. One other question: Did it -- did you in 1999 go to this -- this location with an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor by the name of Ruez?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. You described earlier -- this will be my last series of questions or question. Can you describe for me the other types of arms that were in the column that was moving from Susnjari to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were hunting rifles, pistols, so private hunting rifles and pistols, and automatic weapons, semi-automatic weapons, and Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In your group, let me ask, how many other grenades were there beside the two that you told us about that you had in your position, Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my group no one had a grenade on them. I had two grenades on me, and when we were ambushed in Kamenica or when I was turning around and to crawling, these hand-grenades fell off me. Fortunately, they did not go off. Nobody had anything on them. They didn't have any grenades on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Minor point of clarification. When you state "hunting rifles," do you mean the kind of rifles that one would use to hunt deer or game, big game?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Also within -- grouped within that category of hunting rifles, would you also include shotguns?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, shotguns.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, I thank you very much. I have no further questions at this time. Your Honour, one thing, Mr. President, I was handed an English translation of the article. I don't believe -- I looked at it briefly before Your Honours came in. I don't think I'll have any questions on it, but I just want you to know I'm going to read it when they cross-examine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In fact I was coming to that. I was going to let you finish first. Has the article or the newspaper interview that Madam Faveau referred to yesterday -- I take it now from Mr. Meek that it has been available?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we had one of your attorneys who speaks the language do a quick translation and we've provided that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So, Mr. Zivanovic, would you like to put any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Defence for Mr. Nikolic. Who is going to cross- examine the witness? Madam Nikolic. Madam Nikolic is defending Drago Nikolic in this case. Go ahead. She speaks your own language, so please between question and answer allow a short interval of time, a short pause. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Oric.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Before I put questions to you arising from your testimony yesterday, I would like to clarify something that occurred in the transcript on the 28th of August. On page 56 of the transcript of 28 August you testified that you had recognised a soldier when you were arrested near Konjevic Polje, and you said that he was your neighbour from Studenic and that his name was Gligic or Simic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You testified about this man earlier on in the Blagojevic case, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was that your neighbour who was born in Studenic near Potocari, either in 1968 or 1969?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know him, yes, I had known him from childhood, and he did reside there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He went to school with your sister, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you testified in Blagojevic case on page 1340, the last sentence there -- Gligic, I forgot his first name.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I mentioned his last name. His last name is either Gligic or Simic and I still don't know his name. I asked my sister, but she didn't remember either.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On page 1340 in the Blagojevic trial, you stated clearly that his family name was Gligic. Can we confirm that this man's last name was Gligic, if I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gligic or Simic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you a few questions about the time when you arrived in the territory of Zvornik municipality. You passed through Zvornik and Karakaj. You arrived in the villages of Grbavci and Orahovac and if I'm not mistaken, that was on the 13th of July [as interpreted], 1995, in the afternoon. That's what you said yesterday on page 24 of yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you several questions about the time that you spent in the sports hall during that afternoon. First of all, let me first ask you this: Can you clarify certain facts about Mladic whom you spotted in the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, there has been a mistake in the interpretation, transcript, on page 11, line 6 it says the 13th of July and I believe I mentioned the 14th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You confirmed to my colleague Meek that you saw Mladic with your own two eyes, that he was standing on the doorstep of the sports hall. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecution between the 10th and 12th of August, 1995, you described this event with much greater detail. I suppose this is because the statement was given only a month after the event; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let me read that statement to jog your memory about what you said. "I saw Mladic several times on TV. He did not introduce himself to us. He was surrounded by big body-guards, and at least two of them carried Thompson guns. There were altogether 14 people, including Mladic, his body-guards, and guards who guarded us. Mladic wore a camouflage uniform and his sleeves were rolled up. Mladic is about 173 centimetres tall. He is fat, and he had greying-brown hair." Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you saw Mladic in the sports hall, he did not address your group, did he?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: But he did talk to a person that you thought was commander and you described him yesterday as a tall person in black uniform with sunglasses, and this is on page 27 of yesterday's transcript. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let me go back to one part of your testimony about the events in the sports hall on page 24 of yesterday's transcript. You mentioned that in the sports hall there had been several boys who distributed water to the people there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: These boys brought water to you from time to time and the water would go around until the buckets got empty?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And then if I understood you well, they would leave the sports hall, they would fill up the buckets again, and they would return to continue distributing water in the sports hall. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There was not enough water for all the prisoners, and after some time the conditions in the sports hall were aggravated and people started fainting?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The far end of the sports hall never got any water and they were the ones who suffered the most and they were the ones who fainted.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Throughout that period while you were sitting in the sports hall, there was also the event involving a man who told the others that they shouldn't fret, and they -- and that they should resist.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The same commander spoke to your group and asked you whether anybody else in the group shared that man's opinion?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And that was the same man, the commander, that you described as being tall, wearing a black uniform, having dark hair and dark sunglasses?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Subsequently that same commander returned to the sports hall and that's when the first people were being taken out of the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told us that we would be taken to the Batkovici camp, and that's why we were required to leave the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What we have just discussed happened during the period from the moment you arrived in the sports hall up to the moment sometime in the afternoon when the first prisoners were taken out of the sports hall and loaded on to the vans. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If I have understood you well, in the sports hall under the conditions as they were, you spent some time, some few hours, and you were waiting for the moment when the first prisoners were taken out of the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how long this lasted. I don't know how many hours. I didn't have a watch.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let me just put you one other question. Throughout that period while you were in the sports hall, do you remember that the guards occasionally fired shots in order to calm people down, those people who were in the sports hall? Did they fire shots within the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They fired shots only when that man wouldn't go out. They fired shots in the air, in the sports hall, and they threatened that they would shoot at us if that person refused to leave the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You are a soldier, and I suppose you know. Can you tell us: Was it very noisy in the sports hall when this shooting started? The area was closed.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area wasn't closed. The windows were open. There were windows in the upper part of the walls, so we had windows on three sides. If the room had been closed, that would have -- wouldn't have been normal. Still, it was very noisy. The noise was very strong.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you have any problems with your ears because of that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was not a grenade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you. At one point yesterday during your testimony you mentioned that you had fallen asleep or that you had fainted?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1995, the same one that I had just mentioned, you said that at the moment when you either fell asleep or lost consciousness, that that must have been around 2100 hours?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let me read that part of the statement to you. It is on page 11, in the last sentence. I'd like to jog your memory, and I would like to avoid a situation where I would have to show the statement to you. You said as follows:"I felt dizzy, and after that I either fell asleep or fainted. It may have been around 2100 hours at that point. When I came to, it was dark and it was raining," and I don't want to go on reading your statement back to you. This is part of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is probably a mistake, just like a mistake was done in the transcript when you said "14th" and what entered the transcript was the "13th." I know that that was during the day and not the time mentioned by you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let me show you your statement. This might help us to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have document 3D7 on e- court. This is Mr. Oric's statement in both languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3D7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, but which statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The statement was given to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 10th, 11th, and 12th of August, 1995. This statement was given to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor on those dates. I have hard copies if there are problems with the e-court. Can we also have it in the English for the Trial Chamber, and I would also like the witness to be able to see the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have it on e-court. I mean, we have to find it. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just to assist my colleague in cross-examination, it seems that in the statement of this witness in B/C/S says the date of the interview is 10th, 11th, and 12th of August, 1996, while in English version it says "1995," so just to have this in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you for that. It's definitely as you say. The first page in English with ERN 00336981 certainly does not tally with the first page in B/C/S. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is the same statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing that might have happened when the B/C/S version done the date was altered for some reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That could have -- may well have happened, but the thing is I wouldn't dare say which one is the correct, whether it's the B/C/S one or the English one, because this is August, so -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The date is August of 1995, there's no doubt, and it's simply a typo on the B/C/S translation, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So you know now at least what the Prosecution position is, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we please look at the page 11. Can we have that page on the screen, please. Can the witness be shown that page of his statement, page 11, the last paragraph, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Oric, before you on the screen there is a B/C/S version of your original statement that you gave to the investigators of this Tribunal between the 10th and 12th of August, 1995. You stated here what I just read out to you. Could you please read that statement again and tell me whether this is what you stated at the time.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I now read it aloud? "I was dizzy. After that either I fell asleep or fainted. It may have been around 2100 hours." This is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the English version of this statement on the screen, please? First page of the statement, please, showing the information on the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Oric, your interview lasted three days with the investigators; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You spent three whole days talking about various details of the events that took place on the relevant days. People who were present during the interview were the investigator and the interpreter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You spoke under no pressure or duress and you based your testimony on recollection?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just read out my statement -- the statements that I had given long before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify. This is your statement given in 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And you signed it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And you were interviewed by the investigators for three days. Their names are on the cover page of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The interview lasted just one day.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Just one day?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This means that your statement is actually not your statement, that what we have before us is not your statement at all?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Based on your recollection, on what you could remember at that moment?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that you spoke the truth at the time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there may have been some errors in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go back to one other thing. Can we have document 2094. This is a Prosecution exhibit that was used yesterday by the Prosecution during the direct, and this is the sketch of the area around the school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar is pointing out to me that there are two versions of it. One is the so-called clean version that was provided by the Prosecution the first place; the second is the one on which he put some markings. Which one?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The so-called clean version, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's the clean version, please, and it is 2094.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Can we zoom in just a little bit more, please, can we enlarge the image a bit more, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Oric, my learned colleague asked you about some facts relative to the sketch that you drafted in July 1995 -- I apologise, in August 1995 when you spoke to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the drawing in front of you, and if you look at the third bus from the top, from the school, on the right-hand side there is an arrow and it says "ME," which means "I" or "me" in the Serbian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Who was it who wrote this down? Who put that word on to the sketch?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MO, but it's not very legible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I believe that this is ME.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zoom in, please. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that, but this is MO, but this was done in a haste. I wrote that "MO."

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What's the meaning of this MO?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the place where I was supposed to be killed because of the patch of the Territorial Defence that he had found by the bus. This is where he was supposed to shoot me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You're saying that this word does not mean "I" or "me" in English?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speak English, I don't know. I know that this is where I was sitting and this is where he was supposed to kill me, in front of the bus, at that place. This is where I was sitting, and here by the bus he was supposed to kill me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In other words, these letters, be they ME or MO, were put down by you? You are the one who wrote this? And who was it who wrote down "private house" on the left-hand side where it says "house, house, house, house," four times in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who it was in Tuzla who wrote these words down, who among the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In other words, the markings were made by the investigators?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Tuzla during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In other words, the investigator was the one who pointed to the place where you were supposed to be killed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was the other way around. I showed him and he translated into English.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Madam Nikolic. Mr. Lazarevic, who is -- who will be cross-examining the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic will cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic, Mr. Oric, is defending Mr. Borovcanin. Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall try to clarify some issues and I will try to show you some documents and I will ask for your assistance in explaining some things to us. You've told us that you were born in the village of Lehovici, Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is where you lived, and you've also told us that, "Srebrenica is a small place, we knew each other, all of us there." What was the ethnic structure of the population on the eve of the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I don't know what the ethnic composition was. A majority were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you help us and tell us whether there were any Serbs there and what was their percentage?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Serbs, but I don't know what their percentage was. I was never interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During your professional career before the war you spent some time working in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When was that, what year?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked there from 1985, I worked in Banat, I worked in the sugar plant, I worked in Pancevo in an anti-corrosion plant. I worked for different companies until I joined the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were still under age when you were working in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, one could put it that way, and that was in Banat.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And during your stay in Serbia, did you have any problems with other ethnic groups, ethnic-related problems?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understand, when the war broke out in Croatia you became involved in the conflict between the Croatian forces and the then- JNA?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in Capljina, and it lasted a few days while I was a member of the Croatian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Help us, please, and tell us this: You said that you were a member of the Croatian MUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where is Capljina, in which state?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which state, please?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How come that you as a member of the Croatian MUP found yourself in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were sent there. We had to go there to protect the houses from looting. I had not even known where Capljina was, and when I arrived there it took me only 10 to 15 days to realise where I was. And that's when I left. I abandoned Capljina. I left the post and Capljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Help us, please, and tell us when was that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date, but this must have been sometime in March. I arrived there in February, and in March I left for Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that in February or March 1992 you were in Capljina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be better to say that at the beginning of March I left for Zagreb. I tried to go to Sarajevo; I couldn't. And then I decided to go to Zagreb instead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Had the war started in Bosnia and Herzegovina in February 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know. I was in Zagreb. I did not have enough information as to what was going on. That's why I wanted to go to Tuzla and then to Srebrenica, to see what the situation was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take things one at a time. We are talking about February or beginning of March 1992. I understand that the Croatian MUP sent you to Capljina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your task was to protect the property of the citizens of Capljina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there already war going on in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but the population had moved out of Capljina and they went to Baska Voda and Markaska.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time were there JNA units in Capljina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. They were in the barracks there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any conflicts with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of March, you left and you went to Zagreb. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- actually, I went to Kutina, to my uncle's place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From that moment on, did you stop being a member of the Croatian MUP?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I returned my uniform and my arms, and I went to my uncle's place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that you joined the MUP because of the pay, because of the money that you were paid?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get that money? How much were you paid?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Because my uncle called me and asked me to leave immediately and to come to his place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that you did not get a penny for the time spent in Capljina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point you've told us that you had been trained by the MUP, by the MUP of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was some sort of training in town. This was probably just one part of the entire training -- at least that's what they told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was Nedzad Ibisevic, from the village of Dobrak, born in 1970 just like you, also with us undergoing that training, can you remember that man?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That name doesn't ring a bell, does it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Once you went to Zagreb you say that you joined the army and that you were involved in Orasje?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, how much time did you spend in Orasje?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how much time I spent with my uncle, but he told us that we could go to Ores and we could go to Tuzla. I came to Orasje and I couldn't go any further. We had to stop there to see if it was possible to go on. We had no food and we were told that if we would join the army we would be able to get something to eat. I think I spent full 20 days there, and then we said that we could go to Slavonski Brod. Then we went to Zagreb. There were some trucks. We asked them if they could give us a lift, and we went to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you join in Orasje, which unit?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a Territorial Defence unit. There were more people wearing civilian clothes. I think it was Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is Orasje located in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that you were a member of the HVO or the HV at the time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which army did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were Muslims who lived there. The Territorial Defence which was just assembled in -- throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina. That was at the beginning of the conflict. There was no open conflict at the time. These were units of Territorial Defence. We were not even given rifles. This was simply to get some food, to be able to get some food.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have said -- you have just said: We went in the direction of Brod and then on to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, me and Elvir Mavlic [Realtime transcript read in error "Momir"].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You are referring to you when you say "we"?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript you mentioned Mavlic, Elvir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After you arrived in Tuzla you decided to go to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were demobilised in Tuzla in the Territorial Defence. And I spent some time there in a hotel, I don't remember the name of the hotel, near Banovici. And then I set off for Srebrenica from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, you were demobilised or mobilised in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the benefit of the transcript, this is page 27, line 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for both this one and the previous one, clearing up the name of the person that accompanied him because previously in line 7 it showed Momir, which is completely misleading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Tuzla as member of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina before you set off to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not -- I was not a member of the army but of Territorial Defence. I don't remember how long. I left for Kalesija from there because they told me that there was a way to go to Srebrenica. I spent some 15 days there until a courier came, and then we proceeded to go to Srebrenica. I think it was altogether until June, to Tuzla and Sapna [Realtime transcript read in error "Sabno"]. I don't recall the exact dates. It was sometime in July that I entered Srebrenica. I don't recall the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think there's a transcription error. I believe Sabno is incorrectly transcribed. I think he's referring to another location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, if you could address that. I am not in a position to say if this is right or wrong. In the transcript we have Tuzla and Sabno and it is being said that "Sabno" is not correct. Mr. Oric has heard this now he can clarify it for us. Is it Sabno or some other name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is Sapna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You may move to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when talking about Sapna, at the time of July/August 1992, how big an area was controlled under the Serbian -- the VRS in the area from Tuzla to the area held by the units that defended Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand your question. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will try again. In order to reach Srebrenica at the time, how far did you have to travel that was under the control of the VRS, in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think 20 to 30 kilometres, in the direction that we took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's clear this up. The total distance was what? Total distance of the whole entire journey, you would have covered how many kilometres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The total distance, Your Honour, is more than 150 kilometres. Your Honour, I was asked about the territory under Serbian control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So out of this 100 kilometres plus, 150 kilometres plus, 20 of them or roughly 20 of them were under Serb control. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Since I would tend not to agree with you, Mr. Oric, concerning this point I would ask you again. Could you please state for us which villages - I am talking about July and August 1992 - which villages at that time in the Zvornik municipality were under the control of Territorial Defence or the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zvornica, Kamenica, Lipja, Snagovo, all the way up to the asphalt road. So 20 to 30 kilometres from Snagovo to Nezuk, this territory was under the control of the Serb forces. From Konjevic Polje to Srebrenica, there was an additional 15 kilometres up to Siljkovici and the other part up to Crni Vrh. This is an estimate. I don't think there were more kilometres up to Crni Vrh, from Nezuk to Snagovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you think we can agree that at the time, Kalesija was under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that at the time, Snagovo was under the control of Territorial Defence of the army -- or under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is the army in Srebrenica, but the Zvornik free territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My colleagues suggested that the -- your answer was: Yes, but not under the control of the army from Srebrenica but under the control of the units from Zvornik of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me now show you a document. I would like to ask the registrar to help us for e-court. For your identification this is document that we received under the general collection of the OTP with ERN mark 01007226 to 7227. We marked it as document 4D7. I would like to ask you to have this article shown on the screen, and while we're waiting for this, Mr. Oric, I will put a few questions to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a newspaper interview that you gave to Nedina Dalmacija on the 10th of November, 1995, to Zeljko Garmaz, this journalist named Zeljko Garmaz. For the record, Zeljko Garmaz. Did you, in fact, give this interview?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see this article in the newspaper?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever shown this newspaper article by the OTP in the preparations for this testimony?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask Madam Usher to provide us with a hard copy of this article on the ELMO so that the witness can have a look. Your Honour, if you don't mind, we have underlined a part of the text that we wish to put to the witness in order to save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, irrespective of the fact that you stated that you didn't have an opportunity to read this article, I will put to you the following questions. Will you accept what is stated in the article and then you will be able to say if this interview -- if your memory has been refreshed with regard to this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of Your Honours and the Prosecution, let me just say that we will be using in the English version on the second page the second paragraph at the end of the page. So I think we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that upon your arrival in Srebrenica you were asked by your cousin, Nasir Oric, to go back to Tuzla to get some supplies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is what the text says. Then the text goes on to say --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honour, for the benefit of the identification I would now like to refer to page 2, to the end of the second paragraph in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your version, Mr. Oric, you can see it underlined or highlighted in yellow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber does not have the English version at all. It shows the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have on our monitor the -- what the accused -- what the witness is being shown, but that's about it. And we need an extra copy for ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me to proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So on the second page at the end of the second paragraph it reads: "We stayed in Tuzla for about a month, picked up 47 people, who carried the medication, and headed back for Srebrenica. Nurif Rizvanovic, with 500 armed men, came with us. Our men later liquidated Nurif because he was presumed to be a Serbian spy." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this quote correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct; however, he did not go with us. He went separately from us, accompanied by his troops. He went -- he headed for Srebrenica by his own will with his troops, whereas we had a duty, a mission. And around Crni Vrh, his units suffered losses. So he headed for Srebrenica separately from us. We were led by a courier, and we carried medicines. He went of his own will, and he suffered -- or his men suffered losses around Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please say if you went together or the columns went one behind the other?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we went before, during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So he set out for Srebrenica one day later. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just by the way, how many times were you sent to Srebrenica during that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the first time I went there, and I never went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1993 or 1994, did you take that same road to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Other people went.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "other people went," am I right in thinking that you always take this one beaten track?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they took the same route, I wouldn't be able to tell you. I went one way, and I returned that same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Were you ever decorated as a member of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any recognition from the BiH army after the army or during -- after the war or during the war?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one intervention, Your Honours. One part of Mr. Oric's answer has not been recorded. When he said that Nurif Rizvanovic's men, some seven or eight of them, were killed by mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say that, for the record?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who were the 500 men who joined Nurif Rizvanovic on his way to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never asked anybody. I only know that Professor Sabit [phoen] from Bratunac was killed on that occasion on Crni Vrh. I don't know his family name, and I really don't know who the other men were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they all leave from Tuzla to go to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe this is a good moment for our first break because my next set of questions deals with the period of time covering 1995. So with your leave, kindly let's take this first break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Stojanovic. We'll have a 20-minute break from now. Mr. Bishop will be contacting you. It's in relation to the -- you know what. There's the Prosecution claim that there should be further deletions in the -- in this indictment relating to Tolimir and Trbic. All right. And the deadline, I believe, is today and we need to know what your position is before we proceed with our judgement. 20 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, may we proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to 1995. In the article --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just for the identification, the article that we just had an occasion to see in front of us, in the English version page 2, the beginning of the last paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- it says as follows in our language -- Mr. Oric, I'm reading what it says in the article. "On the eve of the fall of Srebrenica, I was given an order, as I was the commander of a sabotage squad, to look after the UNPROFOR base above the villages of Jaglici and Susnjari." Does this reflect the truth?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the situation like?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The UNPROFOR had left the base. The women stopped them in Jaglici, the women and children. I arrived with my squad and took over that gap that had previously been manned by the UNPROFOR. I came there with my ten men.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the article it says further on, namely: "UNPROFOR troops were trying to escape and we returned them to the base with Zoljas." Help us, please, and help the Trial Chamber and tell us what a Zolja is?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Zolja is a hand-held rocket-launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not there when the UNPROFOR were stopped. The women and the children had left, that is possible, but I wasn't present there with the Zoljas. The women and children stopped the APC, the one APC that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that what it says in the article are not your words?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember ever having stated this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Help us, please, and tell us when was it, what day was it, when the check-point or the observation point of the United Nations was abandoned by the DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 11th July, in the morning. They tried to flee, but the women from Jaglici intercepted them and they couldn't flee. But they did not want to return to the same place. They locked themselves in the APC, and that's where they stayed. They did not dare to move on because they would have had to go over the women and children. That's why I had to go there with my ten men; that was on the 11th, in the morning, when they tried to escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "they tried to escape," does it mean they never left that place?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were on the hilltop above the village, and they had been stopped in the village. The distance is maybe some 2 or 300 metres. First they were on the hilltop, and when they started running away they were stopped and we then took up that position on the hill that they had manned previously. That is an elevation point when they -- that they had held. They tried to escape from there, but they were stopped by the women and children in the village some 2 or 300 metres down the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you properly, they stayed in the village. They were no longer on the hilltop. They were in the village of Jaglici. How long they stayed there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when they left because I did not have an opportunity to see the village. I suppose that when all the people left they left with them, but I don't know when, at what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you couldn't see them, how do you know that they had withdrawn and that you and your unit were supposed to take over that elevation point?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were on the hilltop, and they were at the foot of the hill, in the village. When we were on the hilltop, we could not see the village. I don't know what happened later in the village once I took up the position on the hilltop. I could not see the village of Jaglici from there. That's why I don't know what happened next in the village, whether they left on that same day or whether they left with the rest of the population. I don't know. I did not see them leave the village because I did not have a line of vision from the hilltop to the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before that were you at a point from which you could see their observation point?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in front of the observation point, in front of their observation. Their observation point was behind our backs as well as the village of Jaglici. So we did not have an opportunity to see that. We could only see the area towards Kravica, Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know -- how did you know then that you were supposed to take over the line from which they had withdrawn?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The courier came and told us what had happened. He told us that they had tried to run away and that the line had to be taken over, and there was nobody else there but the ten of us. We were the only ones who could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What unit was that courier from?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From our unit, from the manoeuvre unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are we talking about 283rd Brigade that you've mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What unit is that, your manoeuvre unit?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The manoeuvre company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On whose strength was that manoeuvre company that you're attacking?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the strength of the BiH army, the company that was in that part between Jaglici, Susnjari, Brezovina and during the time when UNPROFOR there or the brigade had been disbanded and the only thing that remained were companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the name of that company?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A manoeuvre company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it known as the 283rd?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I must admit that I am a bit confused. You said that on that day, on the 11th of July, you were resting at home.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was on the line, then we were given free time. The things went like that. You were on the line for 24 hours, and then for 24 hours you were left to go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th, in the morning or in the afternoon, in other words on that day, were you on the line or were you free?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day I was free -- or rather, I was supposed to be free because there was -- there were no troops to man that position. I had to go there with my men to man that position because there were no other men on that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Help us, please. When was it on the 11th, what time of day?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it before noon or in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It may have been either or.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know Ibrahim Mandzic, whose father's name is Idriz?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was he at the time? I'm talking about the year 1995.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what rank he had. I know that he was a commander, but I don't know what was he the commander of.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me help you. He was a major, but I am interested in the unit that he commanded. Do you know what unit was that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. Do you know who -- who --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel please repeat the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, if you could kindly repeat the name because the interpreters couldn't get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. For the record, I was asking about Major Zulfo Tursunovic, whose father's name is Salko. Thank you. I believe that this has been now recorded correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, was he also one of the commanders?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was a commander in Suceska, I suppose so. Most probably he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what unit he commanded?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I am not from Suceska. Suceska is far away from where I was and I don't know. At that time, anybody could be commander, anybody could represent themselves as commander. I don't know. I know that he was one of the persons in charge there with most seniority or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who was Major Ibro Dudic, son of Husein, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have an occasion to meet him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of him?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did in songs. I believe that he hails from Skelani, and that's why I never had any contacts or meetings with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that there were songs about him?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard a song in which he is mentioned as having been killed or gone missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your commander or the head of your unit in 1995, was that Hazim Djanovic, son of Behaija?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, Your Honours, the name is Djanovic Hazim, son of Behaija, B-e-h-a-i-j-a.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not familiar with the name, it doesn't ring a bell. I don't know where that person is from. If he's from Skelani or Osmace, believe me, I don't know many people from there. We did not have any occasion to meet people from there and I don't know him personally and I don't know that he was chief or head. I don't know who the chief was. We are not interested in that. The only thing we were interested in was how to survive the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... because having been here five years this has happened before. Sometimes it's a question of how you pronounce the name of a person, and one letter makes a big difference to the witness. So if it's Hasim instead of Hasib or Hasib instead of Hasim, he will tell you: I don't know. So let's try to be precise. If you don't know, just go on and ask him who his commander was in 1995. But I have had yes and no answers simply on the basis of a letter in a long name which changes. You speak his own language, so I mean you shouldn't have problems in pronunciation, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. When we start talking about names and place names, I shall do that, but let me finish with this and let me mention just one more name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Ejub Golic is?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was he at the time? What was his position or function?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of Glogovac [as interpreted], which is his own place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... again we're talking of 1995. Was he still the commander of Glogova in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether he was there in 1995. Some people had left for Tuzla for additional training. I don't know whether he was at the command post at the time or somebody stood in for him. He was in Tuzla, then he returned. I don't know exactly whether he was there in 1995. In 1992, before the UNPROFOR arrived, he was commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I can be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is the village of Glogova a village that in 1995 was part of the Srebrenica zone or was it under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under the control of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: However, the unit that was under Ejub Golic's command was composed of the villagers of Glogova. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that all these units were on the strength of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The 28th Division, in your knowledge, in addition to the infantry weapons, did it also have artillery pieces and anti-armoured pieces?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did, but without shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that these pieces could not be used?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we just have a time-frame, Your Honour? The time-frame would probably make a difference, I would imagine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I -- thank you. Yes, I would suggest that you precisely do that, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, were we talking about 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe this is the time when I would kindly ask you to allow me to show the witness a video clip that we received from the Prosecution. This is ERN V0004417. This is the ERN on that exhibit, and because of the fact that I still don't have much experience with all this, I would like to provide you with our identification number. This is Defence Exhibit 4D14. But we shall see what your decision is going to be with regard to the procedure with admitting video clips. I would kindly ask the technical booth to provide the witness with a video clip or just a still from the clip that depict events in Srebrenica on the 10th of July, 1995. I repeat, 10 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before -- because you are expecting a decision from us, but before we can decide, do you intend to make use of only one clip from the video or do you intend to put questions on the entire video? Because if you're just going to refer to one clip, we go straight to that clip. If you're going to put questions on the entire video, then we would play the entire video. But the policy here has always been unless there are -- there's an opposition which is a valid one or which is considered to be a valid one, you can bring forward any evidence that is evidently and has probative value.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Our intention is to discuss the 29 minutes of this video clip that we received from the Prosecutor, and we shall focus on just that one segment of this video tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also take it that although you were seeking our go ahead, you were not anticipating any kind of objection on the part of the Prosecution. Are you -- do you have any particular objection to the Defence making use of this video or this still?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. If I understand which video we're talking about, I'm trying to see from our exhibit list whether it is in fact the former Blagojevic Srebrenica trial video, and if that's what it is, we have no objection. That's been used many times before. As long as we have a way of memorialising that particular clip and making sure it's accessible in the record in the future, then we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't help you. Perhaps if the -- if the court staff have managed to locate it, they know exactly which one it is and they can give you the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
